recommendation: Keep the no-change audit commit. Revisit only if BR&R makes a new final decision to require detailed Ingredient.function or to move IngredientFunction terminology to THO.
issue_request: FHIR-26566 is a Published/Persuasive BR&R R5 change request asking to add Ingredient.function as a CodeableConcept for detailed ingredient functions such as antioxidant or alkalizing agent. The Jira description said 1..* and records BR&R approval on 2020-03-24.
initial_application: Commit 35630a55b9ba1df679df5765243f01a2e4162512 explicitly applied FHIR-26566 by adding Ingredient.function to source/ingredient/ingredient-spreadsheet.xml as CodeableConcept 0..*. Later source refactoring moved the resource into source/ingredient/structuredefinition-Ingredient.xml while preserving that optional repeating cardinality, and later commits added the IngredientFunction binding and short-definition cleanup.
additional_context: The current build includes Ingredient as an active BR&R resource. Current source contains Ingredient.function, its example value set/code system, and a token search parameter. The Jira description's 1..* wording does not appear to be a lost source change because the original FHIR-26566 implementation itself used 0..*. A same-day Zulip discussion supports the element's placement in the product-context Ingredient model. Later FHIR-55045 is Submitted/unresolved and only concerns possible THO migration of Ingredient value sets.
reconciliation: No source files were changed. The current active source already carries the requested element and associated implementation surfaces; changing Ingredient.function to 1..* now would be a new conformance change rather than reconciliation of a missed application.

related_jiras.note: Submitted/unresolved later request to consider migrating Ingredient value sets, including ingredient-function, to THO; it does not decide FHIR-26566 cardinality or source placement.
The same historical implementation commit also changed Ingredient strength presentation text for this separate request; it is not part of the Ingredient.function decision.
